answer: At a jetty logistics exchange, agents record allocation ballots in a ledger called quill. Each ballot needs a nonce whose hash, bound to its contents, sender key and current public beacon, meets a fixed difficulty. Validators reject reused tickets. Fresh beacon values prevent stockpiling work for later rounds. Ten thousand fake voters must therefore fund ten thousand puzzles in computation and electricity; extra names provide no free ballots. This assumes secure hashes and cannot stop an attacker with enough computing power.
